overview: The file concerns Japan’s wartime automobile industry and the narrowing position of American manufacturers under Japanese industrial controls. Its principal document is a strictly confidential February 1940 despatch from American Consul Richard F. Boyce reporting that the Ford Motor Company of Japan would suspend production after the government stopped issuing import permits, while Ford, Nissan, and Toyoda considered a jointly owned company capable of supplying Japan and the wider yen-bloc market. The despatch also discusses foreign-exchange restrictions, Ford’s profits and war-bond purchase, and the relationship between the proposed venture and political relations between Japan and the United States. A separate cross-reference sheet points to a March 1940 despatch about Count Aisuke Kabayama’s planned American visit and contacts with Ford and an engineering institute concerning Japan’s motor industry.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Boyce on Ford’s shutdown and proposed Japanese-American automobile venture
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Reports the impending shutdown of Ford’s Yokohama assembly plant and confidential proposals for a Ford-Nissan-Toyoda automobile company.
subfiles.summary: Boyce reports that Japanese authorities will issue Ford no further import permits, forcing its Yokohama assembly plant to close at the end of February and discharge all but a skeleton staff. He describes tentative plans for a new company owned 40 percent by Ford and 30 percent each by Nissan and Toyoda, with Ford initially retaining managerial control and a new plant designed to produce at least 50,000 vehicles annually. The venture could receive privileged access to Japan, Manchukuo, and Japanese-controlled China and might later compete elsewhere in the Far East and Latin America. The despatch also notes Ford’s profits, remitted dividends, purchase of Japanese war bonds, and inability to convert its approximately ¥20 million Japanese investment into American currency.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Grew despatch on Count Kabayama’s American visit
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to a despatch concerning Count Aisuke Kabayama’s planned contacts with Ford and an engineering institute during a visit to the United States.
subfiles.summary: The sheet cross-references original paper number 4555, filed as 033.9411/321 and dated March 6, 1940. That document concerned Count Aisuke Kabayama, a House of Peers member and acting president of the America-Japan Society of Tokyo, and his proposed visit to the United States. Kabayama intended to contact an engineering institute in Pittsburgh and the Ford Company in connection with Japan’s motor-car industry.

interest: The principal despatch offers a detailed contemporary view of how Japanese licensing, foreign-exchange controls, and state-supported manufacturers displaced American automobile assembly operations before the Pacific War. Particularly valuable is the confidential outline of a proposed Ford-Nissan-Toyoda company, including its ownership percentages, anticipated production capacity, intended markets, and dependence on U.S.-Japan relations. The discussion of Ford’s war-bond purchase and trapped Japanese capital illuminates how foreign companies attempted to manage political risk. The Kabayama cross-reference also connects these industrial negotiations to unofficial elite diplomacy and technical contacts in the United States.
